meta.title: Operation of Single Station Tablet Press in Pharmaceutics Laboratory

sections.purpose: To compress granulated or directly compressible pharmaceutical powders into tablets of uniform weight, thickness, hardness, and content as part of formulation development and small-scale production in the Pharmaceutics laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for development and optimization of tablet formulations and preparation of tablet samples for pharmacopeial quality control tests.
procedure: Inspect and clean all die and punch sets before use — check for worn edges, pits, or corrosion; replace damaged tooling.
Install the lower punch, die, and upper punch in the tablet press tooling holder, ensuring secure fitting.
Lubricate punch and die surfaces lightly with approved lubricant (magnesium stearate dusted on surfaces or diluted in IPA solution).
Weigh the granulated/powder blend accurately; record total weight.
Adjust the lower punch depth to the required tablet weight using the weight adjustment knob; verify by ejecting a few tablets and weighing.
Adjust the compression force to achieve the target hardness: set the upper punch descent depth using the hardness adjustment knob.
Compress a series of 10–20 tablets at the initial setting; evaluate for correct weight (± 5% of target per IP), hardness (target range), thickness, and appearance.
Fine-adjust weight and hardness settings as needed after initial evaluation.
Once settings are confirmed, compress the full batch; periodically check tablet weight (every 50–100 tablets) during the run.
Collect all tablets in a labelled, clean container.
After compression, perform in-process quality checks: weight uniformity, hardness, friability, disintegration, and physical appearance.
Disassemble the tooling, clean with a dry brush, then wipe with IPA-dampened cloth; dry and store in tooling boxes.
Clean the die turret and powder contact surfaces with a vacuum and IPA wipe.
Record: blend weight, tablet weight (mean and range), hardness (mean), compression force, and any tablet defects observed.
precautions: Never place fingers near the die-punch area during operation — the compression force (up to several tons) will cause severe crush injury.
Do not operate with damaged, pitted, or corroded punches and dies — defective tooling causes capping, lamination, and sticking.
Ensure all safety guards are in place before starting the press.
Clean thoroughly between different products — cross-contamination is a critical GMP failure.
Do not compress at excessive force — over-compression causes lamination (layers separating) and may damage tooling.
Keep a record of all tooling — track usage and retire worn tooling per manufacturer schedule.
For potent drugs, wear appropriate respiratory protection (N95) and use a closed system or enclosure.
